name: Nebius Group N.V.
monetization: Rents Nvidia GPU cloud capacity under multi-year contracts — ~$46B contracted with Microsoft and Meta — while scaling capex far ahead of current revenue.
description_md: Nebius Group (Amsterdam-headquartered, NASDAQ-listed; the ex-Yandex international business) is Europe's flagship neocloud. In under a year it signed ~$46B of contracted business: up to $19.4B with Microsoft (Sep 2025, five years) and up to $27B with Meta (Mar 2026, five years: $12B dedicated capacity plus up to $15B of additional committed purchases). Nvidia is both its key supplier and a ~$2B equity investor. 2026 guidance: revenue $3.0–3.4B, ARR run-rate $7–9B by year-end, and capex raised from $16–20B to $20–25B on demand — a build program several times current revenue, funded by equity, converts, and vendor-aligned capital.
ai_monetization_md: AI-infrastructure-as-a-service on Nvidia fleets across US and European datacenters (plus adjacent businesses: Toloka data services, TripleTen, Avride autonomy). Revenue is dominated by two anchor take-or-pay-style contracts — Microsoft (up to $19.4B) and Meta (up to $27B) — which convert into recognized revenue as capacity is delivered; 2026 revenue guidance of $3.0–3.4B against ~$46B contracted illustrates the multi-year conversion lag. The Nvidia investment (~$2B, Mar 2026) aligns supply access but adds an equity_for_revenue-adjacent loop: the investor's money helps fund purchases of the investor's chips.
ai_strategy_md: Convert credibility from the two mega-contracts into a diversified customer base before concentration hardens: build fast (capex guide $20–25B for 2026), keep Nvidia alignment for allocation on new architectures, and use the Amsterdam/Europe footprint as a sovereignty selling point for EU AI workloads. The strategic tension is deliberate: accept extreme two-customer concentration now in exchange for scale economics that smaller neoclouds cannot reach, then broaden into enterprise/inference demand.
risk_notes_md: **Customer concentration:** Microsoft and Meta account for the overwhelming majority of the ~$46B contracted backlog; both counterparties have in-house capacity programs and could deprioritize renewals — headline contract values are also 'up to' ceilings, not guaranteed floors (the $27B Meta deal includes $15B of optional additional purchases). **Funding gap:** $20–25B of 2026 capex against $3.0–3.4B of 2026 revenue requires continuous external funding; execution or capital-market disruption directly hits delivery obligations. **Supplier circularity:** Nvidia is supplier and investor (~$2B). **Note:** headline backlog (~$46B) is committed, not realized — realized-to-date sits in quarterly revenue disclosures.
